definition: Small-scale LNG storage facilities used as an alternative to traditional natural gas storage, valued similarly to conventional storage from an investment standpoint.
core_idea: As liquefaction and regasification technology becomes cheaper, small LNG storage facilities let operators buy natural gas during low-demand periods, store it compactly as a liquid, and use or sell it during high-demand ('peak') periods — extending storage capability to locations that lack the geology needed for traditional storage.
key_points: Liquefying gas for storage dramatically shrinks the physical footprint versus traditional storage.
This allows storage in areas without suitable geological formations for conventional natural gas storage.
From an investment standpoint, LNG peak shaving facilities are valued similarly to normal storage facilities.
The basic trading logic is the same as traditional storage: buy/inject during low-demand periods, use/withdraw during heavy-demand periods.
relationships: Alternative to traditional natural gas storage economics
trading_implications: Peak shaving LNG storage can be analyzed like traditional storage — value comes from capturing the spread between low-demand purchase prices and high-demand use/sale value.
